transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-10-07
Time: 15:00 UTC (57 minutes)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Head of ML, Lighthouse), Carlos Vega (CTO), Jenna Park (PM)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
- Lighthouse evaluating open models for multi-lingual content summarization and tool-calling (external search + video metadata).
- Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs: latency, cost, data residency.
- Key asks: 32k/64k context performance, multilingual quality, tool-calling reliability, SOC2/SAML/KMS details.
- Next: Redwood to run benchmarks with customer prompts and share security/compliance artifacts.

Topics: model selection, context-length, multilingual evaluation, tool-calling, deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private), security requirements

Action items (as captured): see metadata above

Transcript Body:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side — I'm Maya, AE for Redwood Inference, and Liam is our SE who will dig into perf.
00:12 Aisha Rahman: Hi, thanks. We're excited. I lead ML at Lighthouse, we do automated video summaries and cross-language indexing.
00:19 Carlos Vega: Carlos here, CTO. Main concerns are cost at scale and data residency for EU customers.
00:24 Jenna Park: Jenna — PM on the content pipeline. We need tool-calling for our search layer, and also structured outputs for timestamps.
00:31 Maya Chen: Great — high level agenda, is: model comparison (open models), context needs (we heard 32k-64k), multilingual quality, tool-calling reliability, and deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private). Any additions?
00:40 Aisha Rahman: No, that's it. Also eager to understand caching and cost control levers.
00:45 Liam Ortiz: Perfect. I'll jump into our recommendations but first can you describe your current stack and constraints? Specifically, where data lives, traffic patterns, and the average/peak document lengths?
00:57 Aisha Rahman: Sure. Content lives in GCP EU regions. Ingest rate about 3k videos a day, spikes 8-10k during events. Average transcript length maps to ~8k tokens, but we have long form interviews that reach ~45k tokens, which is why 64k context interest. Latency SLO for a summary call is 800ms p95 if possible; but for nightly batch it's okay to be higher.
01:20 Carlos Vega: Also we need SOC2 Type II and SAML SSO, and keys must be controllable — KMS integration, ideally customer-managed keys for private deployments.
01:32 Maya Chen: Good — those are standard asks. On the model side, are you prioritizing output quality over cost or vice versa? Or do you want balance?
01:40 Aisha Rahman: For the long-form summarization we prioritize quality even if it's slightly more expensive, but for metadata extraction we want cheaper, faster models. So mixed profile.
01:49 Liam Ortiz: That's common. So our approach is to surface a model catalog with tradeoffs: higher quality base models for long-form summarization (we recommend 32k/64k context variants), and smaller quantized variants for metadata extraction. We also support tool-calling primitives reliably — run book: Redwood's function calling and structured output schema enforcement.
02:05 Jenna Park: Quick question — tool-calling with external search, what's the guarantee around latency and ordering? Last time we tried a few tool chains they were flaky under load.
02:15 Liam Ortiz: Understood. We guarantee at the request routing layer we can pin a request to a single runtime pool with consistent network egress. For heavy tool chains we recommend Dedicated pools so you avoid noisy neighbors — plus we have backpressure and retries at the orchestration layer. In hosted, we do cross-availability-zone routing. There's also an option to run the search as a synchronous call inside your network via VPC peering on Private deployment.
02:40 Aisha Rahman: You mentioned 64k models — which open models do you usually suggest? We've benchmarked some Llama-variants and Mistral but not at 64k.
02:50 Liam Ortiz: We typically recommend a mix: for high-quality summarization, Mistral-AT or Llama family 2 70B context-extended variants (note: some names get butchered in auto transcripts). For 64k specifically, we've been validating community-built context-extension methods and Redwood-verified releases — we also host quantized variants that keep cost down. We can run your prompts through 32k and 64k variants and show ROUGE/BLEU and latency tradeoffs.
03:20 Carlos Vega: How reliable are those community 64k variants? We're worried about hallucination and context-window degradation.
03:28 Liam Ortiz: That's a fair point. Longer contexts can dilute attention if prompt engineering isn't careful. We recommend chunking + KV cache where applicable: keep a rolling vector store of embeddings for retrieval, and use prefix caching for repeated gists. Also we instrument quality — Redwood Optimize flags regressions on evaluation sets.
03:46 Jenna Park: What's the impact on cost when using 64k vs 32k? Do you meter by token?
03:52 Maya Chen: Yes we meter tokens. Roughly speaking, 64k model ops are about 1.6-2x cost depending on batching efficiency. But with batching, prefix caching, and intelligent routing, the per-request unit cost can be reduced. We'll show a modeled cost curve with your expected traffic.
04:08 Aisha Rahman: On multilingual — our content is primarily English but ~25% Spanish, Portuguese, and some Mandarin. Do open models handle these well? We tried a couple of off-the-shelf ones and quality drops.
04:20 Liam Ortiz: Multilingual quality varies by model. Some Mistral forks and Llama variants have decent multilingual fine-tuning. For production we often recommend a small ensemble: a primary model tuned for English, and a language-specific fallback for Mandarin/Portuguese when confidence falls below threshold. Redwood's routing can automatically pick models based on language detectors, and you can set thresholds for when to run a heavier model.
04:45 Carlos Vega: Speaking of routing, can we pin certain customers to Dedicated pools? We need predictable latency for enterprise accounts.
04:51 Maya Chen: Absolutely. Dedicated pools give you reserved capacity, predictable throughput, and network isolation. For the EU residency requirement you can run Dedicated in EU-only zones, or Private (VPC/on-prem) if you need full control and customer-managed keys.
05:05 Aisha Rahman: If we start with Hosted for quick tests and then move to Dedicated, how hard is the migration?
05:12 Liam Ortiz: We built the API and dev workflow to be consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Model version pinning and rollout policies move with you — so staging in Hosted then promoting to Dedicated is relatively smooth. The main differences are networking and key management.
05:25 Jenna Park: Any gotchas with streaming and tool-calling? We rely on streaming partial captions for UX.
05:31 Liam Ortiz: Streaming is supported across our runtimes. Small note: streaming latency is tied to model token generation speed — bigger models will stream slower tokens per second but we support chunked streaming and early return heuristics for structured outputs, so UX remains snappy.
05:48 Aisha Rahman: Security questions: do you have SOC2, ISO, SAML docs to share? Also need encryption at rest with customer keys.
05:56 Maya Chen: Yes. We will share SOC2 and ISO summaries and our SAML SSO integration guide. For key management, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. We'll attach links in the follow-up.
06:07 Carlos Vega: Can you run benchmarks against our sample dataset? We need p95 latency and quality on our long interviews.
06:13 Maya Chen: Yes — that's one of the next steps. Could you share a sanitized sample and prompt sets?
06:18 Aisha Rahman: I'll get 3 prompt sets today. Expect a short set for metadata, a medium for highlight extraction, and a long-form summarization set.
06:26 Liam Ortiz: Great. For the benchmarks we'll run against 4 candidate model families: 1) high-quality 32k variant, 2) extended 64k candidate, 3) smaller quantized 8-16k for metadata, 4) a multilingual fallback model. We'll return latency, token cost, and quality metrics.
06:45 Jenna Park: On the quality metrics — do you measure hallucination? We need structured fact-checks back to source timestamps.
06:53 Liam Ortiz: We can run custom evals. For hallucination we surface citation matching against the transcript and report recall/precision for facts. Our console exposes per-prompt quality scores and regression alerts.
07:09 Carlos Vega: Any competitors we should be aware of in terms of feature parity?
07:13 Maya Chen: The ones that come up often are Anthropic for safety-focused models, OpenAI for large multimodal and easy-to-use endpoints, and Cohere for embeddings/ML infra. But our value prop is unified runtime + deployment modes + cost controls.
07:28 Aisha Rahman: Budget question — if we want Dedicated for EU-only with reserved capacity for peak usage, what's a ballpark?
07:36 Maya Chen: I'll put together a tailored pricing model but ballpark, Dedicated reserved pools start in the low tens of thousands per month for a small pool; enterprise commit scales with slots and SLAs. We'll send an initial estimate in the model perf matrix.
07:49 Liam Ortiz: Also note there are autoscaling burst policies to contain peak cost — you can set hard caps and fallback routing to cheaper models.
08:00 Jenna Park: One more question — tool-calling reliability: if a call to external search times out, do you have automated retry semantics or fallback to an internal KB?
08:09 Liam Ortiz: Yes, we allow orchestration-level policies: retries, exponential backoff, and fallbacks to cached retrievals. You can configure per-route. We'll share docs.
08:22 Aisha Rahman: Sounds good. Curious about quantization: have you seen quality regressions for our use cases?
08:29 Liam Ortiz: For extraction tasks, quantized 4-bit variants often maintain acceptable quality; for nuanced long-form summary they can lose subtlety. That's why we'll test both.
08:38 Maya Chen: Quick recap: Redwood will run a benchmark suite on your sample prompts across 4 model candidates, measure p95 latency, cost per request, and quality metrics (ROUGE, hallucination checks). We'll share SOC2/ISO/SAML/KMS docs and a pricing/architecture proposal. Lighthouse provides sample prompts and data.
08:56 Carlos Vega: Timeline?
09:00 Maya Chen: We'll send the model matrix and pricing by 2026-10-09; Liam will deliver benchmarks by 2026-10-14; follow-up meeting week of 2026-10-16.
09:10 Aisha Rahman: Works. Anything else?
09:13 Jenna Park: No, thanks. Appreciate the clarity.
09:16 Maya Chen: Thanks all — I'll share notes and links after.
09:20 [call ends]
